answer: Coordinated Harbor Pricing. Every agent action pays a fee proportional to the mutual information between its declared coordination set and prior sets seen this epoch. Isolated actors pay near zero; clusters whose members repeatedly co-act incur multiplied costs, as when signals overlap across a nebula of weakly linked nodes. Each identity therefore carries an ongoing cost tied to how tightly it couples with others. Attackers must spread a tundra of expensive uncorrelated accounts, making mass sybil capture economically unviable.
